column3: Graves disease with severe ophthalmopathy is best treated surgically (now usually total thyroidectomy); radioiodine can worsen the eye disease and drugs alone often relapse.
Catecholamine excess is confirmed biochemically first (plasma free or 24-h urinary metanephrines; here 24-h urinary VMA/noradrenaline), then the tumour is localised by CT/MRI.
A pulsatile mass at the carotid bifurcation that moves side to side but not up and down is a chemodectoma (carotid body tumour); duplex/CT angiography, then excision.
Firm, rubbery fusiform lumps that tingle on pressure lie along a nerve: neurofibromas (benign nerve sheath tumours).
Hypothyroid features with a firm rubbery goitre and lymphocytic infiltrate with lymphoid follicles on FNA is Hashimoto thyroiditis.
Capsular and vascular invasion on histology (not cytology) is what distinguishes follicular carcinoma from follicular adenoma.

A 22-year-old anxious woman has a month’s history of worsening diarrhoea and has lost 10 pounds despite a good appetite. She has a slight tremor, an irregular pulse of 110/min and a bruit over the thyroid, with no obvious deformity or palpable nodes.
